article.title: Google WeatherNext 3直接使用即時衛星資料，全球AI天氣預報每小時更新
article.summary: Google推出全球AI天氣模型WeatherNext 3，開始直接使用每小時更新的地球同步衛星觀測資料，搭配既有大氣分析資料產生預報。模型可每小時依最新觀測重新預報，部分地表氣象資料解析度最高達5公里，目前已用於Google搜尋、Gemini、Google Maps及Google Cloud等服務。

article.title: Gemini could take a page from ChatGPT’s book for this design update
article.summary: TL;DR The Google Gemini app is testing a couple of design updates, specifically for the camera interface and the @ menu. Interestingly, the under-development camera interface appears to be inspired by the ChatGPT mobile app. Meanwhile, the @ menu refresh could make it cleaner while also hiding disabled Connected Apps from view. The Google Gemini app’s overall UI has changed a fair bit over the past couple of years, and all signs point to more changes coming up. We recently spotted design tweaks to the Gemini Live interface , and can now report on a possible refresh of the app’s camera UI, along with a significant overhaul of the ‘@’ menu. article.title: Meta is paying to peek at how you use their latest AI model
article.summary: For its new Muse Spark model, intended for operating coding and other agents, Meta is offering an explicit discount averaging out to about 95% for users who "contribute" to the development of future models by sharing their prompts and model outputs.

article.title: Google wants to let you use your phone as a remote Googlebook trackpad
article.summary: TL;DR Googlebook laptops are arriving soon, featuring heavy cross-connectivity with Android phones. Users will be able to cast apps from phones to their Googlebook in order to remotely interact with them. It now appears that we’ll also be able to control Googlebooks remotely by using phone touchscreens as a trackpad. Do you ever think of your phone as a remote control? We already use our phones to control countless other devices through the apps they connect to, but somehow that feels like a different class of interaction entirely. article.title: Your older Pixel phone may finally be getting Quick Share AirDrop support
article.summary: TL;DR Android picked up cross-platform Quick Share/AirDrop support last fall, but access has been limited to specific device models. On the Pixel front, that’s included phones from the Pixel 8a on up, but earlier today we learned of a possible expansion to the Pixel Tablet. We’re now also getting reports of Pixel 7 and Pixel 8 users seeing notifications of this new support. Devices that won’t play nicely together suck . Sometimes incompatibility is the design goal, trying to lock you into one ecosystem or another. Other times it’s a glitch, or even just developer callousness. But however it starts, we’re always glad to see it come to an end.
